rationale: C04 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. It assigns telecommunications planning and radio-frequency functions under section 305 of the Communications Act, calls for coordinated emergency plans that maximize national security while minimizing interference with nongovernmental requirements, and preserves FCC jurisdiction. The child develops that same framework into detailed FCC and agency plans for controlling government and nongovernment radio emissions during attack while preserving normal operations where practicable. C12 has a weaker parallel involving emergency control combined with preservation of ordinary private operations, while C14 supplies only a more general delegation-and-coordination model.

shared_material.child_excerpt: plans be prepared and implemented whereby government and non-government radio stations may be silenced or required to be operated in a manner consistent with the needs of national security and defense
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Coordinating the development by the several agencies of the executive branch of telecommunications plans and programs designed to assure maximum security to the United States in time of national emergency
shared_material.explanation: Both prescribe coordinated telecommunications planning for national-security emergencies.

shared_material.child_excerpt: it is desirable, so far as possible and practicable, to preserve and maintain normal conditions and relationships under which such radio stations are operated
shared_material.parent_excerpt: with a minimum interference to continuing nongovernmental requirements
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts C04's balancing principle: emergency telecommunications security should disrupt ordinary nongovernmental activity as little as practicable.

shared_material.child_excerpt: pursuant to the authority vested in the President by section 305 of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended, prepare and put into effect such plans
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Assigning radio frequencies to Government agencies under the provisions of section 305 of the Communications Act of 1934, as amended
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same statutory radio-frequency authority as part of an interagency telecommunications mechanism.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Nothing in this order shall be construed as authorizing the Commission to exercise any authority with respect to the content of station programs.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Nothing in this order shall be deemed to impair any existing authority or jurisdiction of the Federal Communications Commission.
shared_material.explanation: Both expressly delimit the new telecommunications machinery to preserve the FCC's established regulatory sphere.
